question: Why is it so tricky to make drugs that kill parasites without harming human patients?

options.A: Parasites share a similar eukaryotic cell structure with human hosts
options.B: Human immune systems cannot produce antibodies against parasites
options.C: Parasites replicate much faster than bacterial pathogens
options.D: Antiparasitic medications are always destroyed by stomach acid

explanation: You've got this! Because both human cells and parasites are eukaryotic (complex cells with a nucleus), it's tough to design a medicine that attacks the parasite without hurting our own cells. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h1)

question: Which of these terms describes multicellular parasitic worms?
explanation: Spot on! Helminths are multicellular worms (like tapeworms and roundworms). Protozoa are tiny and single-celled, while ectoparasites hang out on the outside of the skin. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h1)

question: How do benzimidazole medications primarily get rid of parasitic worms in the gut?

options.A: By increasing calcium levels to cause permanent muscle spasm
options.B: By blocking glucose uptake and depleting energy stores
options.C: By binding directly to bacterial cell walls in the gut
options.D: By dissolving the outer protective skin of the worm

explanation: Think of it as cutting off the worm's food supply! Benzimidazoles stop the parasite from absorbing glucose, so it runs out of energy and dies. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h2)

question: A patient takes praziquantel for a tapeworm infection. What is a normal thing you'd expect to see afterwards?

options.A: Passage of dead or paralyzed worms in traveler's stool
options.B: Sudden spike in blood pressure and rapid weight gain
options.C: Complete cessation of urine output due to kidney injury
options.D: Severe hair loss within twenty-four hours of the dose

explanation: Don't be startled! Praziquantel paralyzes the worm, which means the patient will pass the immobile or dead worms safely out through their stool. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h2)

question: What is the main way chloroquine fights against the malaria parasite?

options.A: Stimulating the spleen to produce extra red blood cells
options.B: Destroying the cell wall using strong digestive enzymes
options.C: Blocking the mosquito from biting the human skin
options.D: Preventing the detoxification of heme inside the parasite

explanation: Great job! When the malaria parasite eats hemoglobin, it creates a toxic byproduct called heme. Chloroquine stops the parasite from neutralizing it, so the parasite essentially poisons itself. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h3)

question: Why must nurses check for G6PD deficiency before giving a patient primaquine?

options.A: To prevent severe hemolytic anemia in vulnerable patients
options.B: To confirm the liver is strong enough to process the drug
options.C: To ensure the patient does not have a concurrent bacterial infection
options.D: To check if the patient is already immune to malaria

explanation: Safety first! Patients with G6PD deficiency lack the protection needed to keep their red blood cells stable against primaquine, which can trigger dangerous red blood cell breakdown (hemolysis). [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h3)

question: What common side effects of metronidazole should you warn your patient about so they don't panic?

options.A: Permanent yellowing of the skin and eyes
options.B: Complete loss of the sense of smell
options.D: Sudden swelling of the hands and feet

explanation: A metal taste in the mouth and darker urine can look scary to a patient, but it's totally normal with metronidazole. Giving a quick heads-up saves them a lot of worry! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h4)

question: A patient on metronidazole asks if they can take a small drink of alcohol with dinner. What should you tell them?

options.A: Wait until you finish the full course of pills, and then you can drink alcohol immediately.
options.B: Avoid alcohol entirely during treatment and for three days after stopping the drug.
options.C: Alcohol is completely safe with this medicine, but it might make you feel sleepier.
options.D: You may drink small amounts of alcohol as long as you take the medication with food.

explanation: Mixing alcohol and metronidazole causes a terrible reaction with severe vomiting, flushing, and racing heart rate. Always remind patients to skip the drinks until a few days after finishing the meds! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h4)

question: How does permethrin cream work against skin bugs like scabies mites and lice?

options.A: By blocking their ability to absorb oxygen through the skin
options.B: By dissolving the outer exoskeleton through extreme acidity
options.C: By stimulating the immune system to attack the eggs
options.D: By disrupting sodium channels and causing paralysis

explanation: Permethrin messes up the nerve signals in the bug's sodium channels, freezing their muscles so they become paralyzed and die. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h5)

question: If one person in a house has scabies, why is it super important to treat everyone living in that home at the same time?

options.A: Mites spread easily through close personal contact and shared bedding
options.B: Topical creams expire quickly once opened in a shared household
options.C: Family members always develop symptoms faster than the index patient
options.D: Untreated family members will develop permanent skin scarring

explanation: Scabies mites love to hop between people through skin contact or shared blankets. Treating the whole household at once stops everyone from passing the bugs back and forth! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h5)

question: Why do nurses need to check a patient's other medications when starting an antiparasitic drug that goes through the liver?

options.A: Liver enzymes completely neutralize the therapeutic effect of all parasites
options.B: Patients with liver issues cannot absorb any form of topical cream
options.C: Many antiparasitic drugs are metabolized by liver enzymes, altering blood levels
options.D: Hepatic enzymes prevent gastrointestinal side effects entirely

explanation: The liver handles many of these drugs. If another medicine speeds up or slows down those liver enzymes, it can accidentally cause drug toxicity or make the treatment fail. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h6)

question: Which side effect tends to happen with almost all oral antiparasitic medications?

options.A: Sudden yellowing of the skin and sclera
options.B: Gastrointestinal upset like nausea and cramps
options.C: Severe hair loss within the first week
options.D: Permanent hearing loss in high frequencies

explanation: Most oral antiparasitic drugs are a bit rough on the stomach lining, often leading to mild nausea, stomach cramps, or tummy discomfort. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h6)

question: What is the biggest risk if a child receives the wrong, uncalculated dose of an antiparasitic drug?

options.A: Under-dosing can cause treatment failure and drug resistance
options.B: Incorrect doses prevent topical creams from working
options.C: Weight-based dosing only matters for intravenous antibiotics
options.D: Over-dosing always leads to permanent blindness

explanation: Always double-check those pediatric weights! Giving too little medication might leave some hardy parasites alive, helping them bounce back stronger and drug-resistant. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h7)

question: What key tip should you give a patient about finishing their prescribed antiparasitic pills?

options.A: Share the remaining medication with family members who feel itchy
options.B: Complete the entire course of medication even if symptoms disappear
options.C: Double the next dose if you forget to take one pill on time
options.D: Stop taking the pills as soon as your stomach starts feeling better

explanation: Even if the patient starts feeling 100% better, remind them to finish every single pill. Stopping early means some parasites might still be hiding out ready to cause a comeback! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h7)
